exercise.title: The diminished 7 chord
exercise.why: A diminished 7 chord is minor 3rds stacked all the way round, so every note of it sits the same distance from the next and each one is a half step under a chord it can lead to.

cells.text:
Bdim7 is the diminished triad, {{1}} {{b3}} {{b5}}, with one more minor 3rd on top. That top note is a diminished 7th above the root, and the staff below draws it as {{6}}, which is the same pitch.
Tap the four notes up from the low {{1}}, then tap on to the high {{1}}: that last step is a minor 3rd too.
Practice until the four even steps sound like one chord to you.

Press Play below to start the backing track: two bars of Bm7♭5, the half-diminished chord, then two bars of Bdim7. Only the top note differs: it is a half step lower in Bdim7.
Practice until you can call out the bar where the chord changes with your eyes off the chord boxes.

Press Play below to start the backing track: a diminished 7 chord, then {{chord:I}}, then the same diminished 7 chord and {{chord:i}}. Both times the root of the diminished 7 chord sits a half step under home.
Practice until you hear home coming a bar early.
{{?key}}In another key the chords have other names, and the diminished 7 chord still sits a half step under home.
